summary: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) is a working multi-storey market near Chiang Mai’s Ping River. Its upper levels are a worthwhile browse for fabric by the metre, clothing, indigo and hill-tribe textiles, tailoring, bags and household goods; the ground floor is mainly food. This is a shopping-focused slice of the larger market visit.
whyGo: Browse everyday textiles and clothing in a busy local market rather than a curated craft shop.
See the market’s upper galleries and pair them with food stalls downstairs or adjacent Ton Lam Yai flower market.
bestFor: Travelers interested in fabric, clothing, homewares and everyday Chiang Mai commerce.
A flexible daytime stop near the Old City and Ping River.
skipIf: You need a reliably step-free route to every floor or wide, quiet aisles.
You are seeking a polished boutique experience or have no interest in shopping.
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for the upper floors; around 1–2 hours if browsing the main market too. Planning estimates, not published timings.
cost: No admission charge is indicated. Purchases and tailoring are extra; stall prices vary, so ask before committing. No reliable current price list found.
hours: The market generally operates daily from early morning to late afternoon, with published schedules varying and individual stalls keeping their own hours. Aim for daytime and verify locally before a special trip.
bestTime: Morning through early afternoon, when the market is active and shops are more likely to be open. Weekday mornings may be calmer; this is local-guide advice, not a guaranteed crowd pattern.
gettingThere: Warorot Market is on Wichayanon Road in the Kad Luang district, about 1.3 km (15–20 minutes on foot; estimate) from Tha Phae Gate. Walk, take a local songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail; ask for Kad Luang or Warorot Market.
booking: No booking or entry ticket is indicated; browse independently. Ask tailoring shops about completion time before ordering, especially on a short stay.
accessibility: Access is not formally documented. A recent local guide reports an escalator from the ground floor to floor 2 (the first level above street level) since October 2025, with stairs elsewhere; a lift was not confirmed. Narrow, crowded aisles may be difficult for wheelchairs or pushchairs. Check conditions locally if access is essential.
practicalTips: Thai floor numbering counts the ground floor as floor 1, so floor 2 means the first level above the street.
Look for fabric sold by the metre, indigo clothing, embroidered textiles, bags and household goods; stall mix can change.
Carry small cash, compare items and confirm the price and any tailoring timeline before purchase.
Ask before photographing sellers or stalls, and keep valuables secure in crowded aisles.
decemberNotes: A flexible daytime shopping stop for December 2026; no special seasonal event or holiday schedule was confirmed. Exact opening hours and stall availability that far ahead are uncertain, so check close to the visit. Year-end traffic may affect travel time; allow a buffer as a planning precaution.
uncertainties: No official upper-floor directory, complete floor plan, current stall-level prices or confirmed lift information was found.
Hours vary between published sources and individual vendors; December 2026 opening arrangements are not confirmed.
Escalator and floor details come from a recent local visitor guide and may change.
